articles.title: AI Buildout Overtakes Housing as America's Top Investment Engine
articles.excerpt: Real spending on data centers and computer hardware hit $752 billion in the second quarter, surpassing residential investment for the first time — a milestone that shows where the economy's confidence now sits.
articles.image_caption: A data center facility. AI infrastructure buildout has overtaken housing as America's top investment engine.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-Americans are heavily represented in the technology sector driving this buildout, from hyperscaler engineering teams to data-center construction and semiconductor supply chains, making the shift a direct read on the industry many in the community work in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Stock Futures Edge Up After Dow's Third Straight Weekly Loss
articles.excerpt: Index futures pointed to a modestly higher open early Monday as investors steadied after the Dow's worst week since March, with oil prices and the coming Trump-Xi summit setting the week's tone.
articles.image_caption: The trading floor of the New York Stock Exchange.
articles.nri_angle: Many Indian-American households hold diversified U.S. equity exposure through 401(k)s and brokerage accounts, so a volatile September shaped by rates and oil prices directly affects year-end retirement balances.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Blackstone Says India Is Nearing a Tipping Point for Foreign Capital
articles.excerpt: Jon Gray told Bloomberg Television that India now generates Blackstone's best private-equity returns in the world — a reversal from the years it "did basically nothing" there.
articles.image_caption: A Blackstone sign stands outside one of the firm's offices. Blackstone executives say India is nearing a tipping point for foreign capital inflows.
articles.nri_angle: For NRI investors weighing India allocations, Blackstone's verdict reframes the trade: the world's largest alternative asset manager says India has moved from a long-dated demographic promise to its best-performing private-equity market on actual returns.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI's Wobbly House of Cards Is Now a Risk to Markets and the Economy
articles.excerpt: Circular deals between OpenAI, Nvidia and Oracle have funded a $1 trillion AI buildout. Now credit markets are questioning who can actually pay for it.
articles.image_caption: The New York Stock Exchange. Analysts warn the AI trade's wobbly valuations are becoming a risk to markets and the broader economy.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian and diaspora investors with heavy exposure to U.S. tech stocks, index funds and Big Tech debt, the AI financing chain is now a portfolio-level risk, not just a tech story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Fed Delivers First Rate Hike Since 2023 as Sticky Inflation Meets a Stronger Economy
articles.excerpt: The Federal Reserve lifted its benchmark rate to 3.75%–4.00% in a unanimous vote, arguing a resilient economy gives it room to attack inflation it now says won't reach 2% until 2029.
articles.image_caption: The Marriner S. Eccles Federal Reserve Board Building in Washington, D.C. The Fed delivered its first rate hike since 2023 amid sticky inflation.
articles.nri_angle: Higher-for-longer U.S. rates support dollar strength and elevated bond yields — relevant for NRIs holding U.S. cash, fixed-income investments, and remittance timing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India set for 'unparalleled' decades-long growth, says Tata chief Chandrasekaran
articles.excerpt: Speaking at Sai University's convocation in Chennai, the Tata Sons chairman said AI would create industries that don't exist today and told graduates to treat careers as marathons — while arguing India's economic rise could run for decades.
articles.image_caption: N Chandrasekaran, chairman of Tata Sons, speaks at a podium against a purple backdrop. Addressing Sai University's convocation in Chennai, he said India is entering a period of economic growth unparalleled in its history.
articles.nri_angle: The Indian diaspora weighs investing and building back home against opportunities abroad, and Chandrasekaran's decades-long India growth outlook frames where that overseas capital and talent flow next.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's exports to China jump 39% as core BRICS shipments rise 34% to $19.9 billion
articles.excerpt: Commerce ministry data show shipments to China, South Africa, Brazil and Russia reached $19.9 billion in the first five months of the fiscal year, lifting the bloc's share of India's export basket to 9.2%.
articles.image_caption: A container ship loads cargo at the Hai Phong International Container Terminal. India's exports to China rose 39% in April–August 2026-27 on engineering goods, electronics and petroleum products.
articles.nri_angle: India's record export run and its growing BRICS footprint strengthen the rupee's earnings base, which supports NRI remittance value and diaspora investment confidence.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Saudi Arabia exits China-led mBridge currency platform in blow to de-dollarization push
articles.excerpt: Riyadh's central bank says it completed its proof of concept in May 2025 and never intended to stay; the quiet exit, reported by the Financial Times, removes the world's top oil exporter from a system built to sidestep the dollar.
articles.image_caption: A 10-riyal note issued by the Saudi Arabian Monetary Agency. The Saudi Central Bank has withdrawn from the mBridge currency platform after completing its pilot in May 2025.
articles.nri_angle: The millions of Indian workers in the Gulf who send money home depend on dollar-denominated settlement networks, so Saudi Arabia's exit keeps that familiar remittance plumbing dominant for now.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NRIs Can Shift NRO Funds to NRE Accounts Up to $1 Million a Year - With New Form 145/146 Paperwork
articles.excerpt: Under RBI's FEMA rules the USD 1 million annual cap is unchanged, but the Income-tax Act, 2025 renamed the transfer paperwork: old Form 15CA is now Form 145 and Form 15CB is now Form 146 - a transition wrinkle that can delay transfers.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee notes. NRIs can now shift up to $1 million a year from NRO accounts to NRE accounts.
articles.nri_angle: This is core diaspora personal finance: NRIs with Indian rental income, dividends or property-sale proceeds routinely need to repatriate, and the form renaming is exactly the detail that trips up filers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Replacing Russian Barrels Will Hike Costs for Indian Refiners, Industry Warns
articles.excerpt: With Trump having signed the Russia sanctions law authorising up to 100% tariffs on top buyers of Russian oil, India's refiners face costlier spot cargoes, freight and insurance - just as Russian crude hit a record 55% share of imports.
articles.image_caption: Indian refiners warn costs will rise as they replace discounted Russian barrels with alternative crude supplies.
articles.nri_angle: US-based readers have direct skin in this game: tariffs of up to 100% on Indian goods would raise prices on Indian exports to the US and strain the US-India economic relationship.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: EPF Wage Ceiling Raised to Rs 25,000 After 12 Years: What It Means for Your Take-Home Pay
articles.excerpt: Effective September 17, 2026, mandatory PF coverage extends to workers earning up to Rs 25,000 a month - adding about 51 lakh employees to EPFO but cutting take-home pay by up to Rs 1,200 for those previously capped.
articles.nri_angle: Relevant for NRIs relocating back to India who take Indian payroll jobs - the higher ceiling changes offer-negotiation math.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jewellers Face Higher Hallmarking Costs as Festive, Wedding Demand Picks Up
articles.excerpt: The BIS raised the gold hallmarking fee 67% to Rs.75 per article from September 14, just as buying season begins — and jewellery stocks slid on the news.
articles.image_caption: A jeweller displays gold necklaces and earrings at a store in India. Hallmarking costs are rising for jewellers as festive and wedding-season demand picks up.
articles.nri_angle: The hike lands in wedding and festive buying season, when many NRIs purchase gold in India, adding a fixed compliance layer to lightweight pieces in particular.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Software Exports Jump 8.2% to $221.4 Billion as US Share Grows
articles.excerpt: The RBI's annual survey shows American clients now account for 54.1% of exports, with total receipts including overseas operations hitting $239.3 billion.
articles.image_caption: Employees work at desks inside an Indian IT services office. India's software exports rose 8.2% to $221.4 billion in FY26, with the US share growing, according to an RBI survey.
articles.nri_angle: Deepening US concentration means Indian IT's fortunes — and those of Indian tech workers and investors exposed to the sector — are tied to American corporate technology spending.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gold hits one-week high, set for weekly gain as oil slide eases inflation fears
articles.excerpt: Spot gold rose 1.2% to $4,390.11 an ounce on Friday, its highest since September 11, as a third straight drop in crude prices cooled inflation worries — though a strong dollar and hawkish central banks capped gains.
articles.image_caption: Gold bars. Gold touched a one-week high as sliding oil prices eased inflation pressure.
articles.nri_angle: Physical gold demand in India was subdued this week as buyers held back in anticipation of lower prices, a soft patch that could translate into keener retail rates for diaspora households ahead of festival and wedding-season buying.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air India Combined Loss More Than Doubles to ₹22,238 Crore in FY26
articles.excerpt: Tata Group-owned Air India and Air India Express posted a record combined net loss as revenue slipped 9%, with chairman N. Chandrasekaran framing the turnaround as a five-to-ten-year journey.
articles.image_caption: An Air India Airbus A320neo in the airline's new Tata-era livery taxis on a runway. Air India and Air India Express reported a record combined net loss of ₹22,238 crore in FY26, more than double the previous year's loss.
articles.nri_angle: Air India is the primary carrier connecting millions of overseas Indians to home; its financial strain and turnaround shape fares, network reliability, and Gulf/UK/North America connectivity for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shapoor Mistry Backs Tata Sons Listing as RBI Directive Clears Path
articles.excerpt: The Shapoorji Pallonji Group chairman welcomed the Reserve Bank's refusal to let Tata Sons deregister as an NBFC, calling a public listing a bridge between private ownership and public accountability amid a deepening boardroom rift.
articles.image_caption: The Shapoorji Pallonji Engineering and Construction building in Hyderabad. Group chairman Shapoor Mistry welcomed the RBI’s September 11 decision pushing Tata Sons toward a public listing.
articles.nri_angle: Tata group equities and ADRs sit in many Indian-diaspora portfolios, so a clearer regulatory path and stronger holding-company governance directly affect the value of those investments.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rentomojo debuts at 19% premium, then rallies further on NSE
articles.excerpt: The furniture-rental platform opened at ₹482.45, a 19.42% premium to its ₹404 IPO price, and climbed to ₹526.70 within an hour; the ₹1,255.57-crore issue was subscribed nearly 73 times.
articles.image_caption: Coverage of Rentomojo's market debut. The furniture-rental platform opened at Rs 482.45 on the NSE — a 19.42% premium over its Rs 404 IPO price — and rallied about 9% further within the first hour of trade.
articles.nri_angle: Rentomojo's debut sets the benchmark valuation for India's rental-economy sector and signals to global investors how the Indian consumer subscription market is being priced.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Goldman Sachs Now Sees Fed Hiking Rates Again in October
articles.excerpt: After calling an end to the Fed's tightening cycle, Goldman reverses course and forecasts a consecutive 25-basis-point increase — while the bank's own asset-management arm bets on a skip until December.
articles.image_caption: A Federal Reserve official speaks at a podium during a press briefing in Washington. The central bank raised its policy rate to 3.75%-4.00% this week, and Goldman Sachs now forecasts a second consecutive 25-basis-point hike at the October meeting.
articles.nri_angle: A consecutive October hike would raise borrowing costs for Indian diaspora households in the US while strengthening the dollar against the rupee, with knock-on effects on remittances, NRI deposits, and India's own rate decisions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gold at $10,000 'Entirely Feasible', AI Trade Faces 'Implosion': Jefferies' Chris Wood
articles.excerpt: In a CNBC-TV18 interview, Jefferies' Chris Wood laid out a scenario where US yield suppression sends gold past $10,000, warned of 'massive capital destruction' from AI spending, and called India a 'reverse AI trade' poised to benefit.
articles.image_caption: Christopher Wood, global head of equity strategy at Jefferies. Wood says gold at $10,000 an ounce is 'entirely feasible' and warns the AI capex boom could end in 'massive capital destruction.'
articles.nri_angle: Wood's thesis ties two of the biggest market debates directly to Indian households and portfolios: a gold surge would massively enrich Indian savers, and an AI-trade reversal would bring foreign flows back to Indian equities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gold Rebounds Above $4,300 as Dollar Eases and Investors Digest Fed Hike
articles.excerpt: Spot bullion rose more than 1% to $4,310 an ounce on Thursday, bouncing off a near six-week low as easing oil prices and a softer dollar offset the Fed's hawkish rate increase.
articles.image_caption: Gold bars at a refinery. Spot gold climbed more than 1% to $4,310 an ounce, rebounding as the dollar eased and investors digested the Federal Reserve's rate hike.
articles.nri_angle: Gold trading near record highs continues to add value to the jewelry and savings held by Indian households, among the world's largest holders of bullion.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Fed Raises Rates for First Time in Three Years, Defying Trump's Demand for Cuts
articles.excerpt: In a unanimous 12-0 vote, Chairman Kevin Warsh led the Federal Reserve's first rate increase since July 2023, lifting the benchmark to 3.75%-4% to fight inflation running near 4% — and signaling one more hike before year-end.
articles.image_caption: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks at a press conference in Washington. The Fed raised its benchmark rate to 3.75%-4% on Wednesday, its first increase in more than three years.
articles.nri_angle: Higher US rates and a stronger dollar pressure the rupee and emerging-market assets, affecting NRI portfolios, remittance values, and dollar-denominated borrowing costs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NRI Deposit Surge Drives India's July Balance of Payments to $20.8B Surplus
articles.excerpt: Capital account inflows hit $27.7 billion as the RBI's deposit schemes pulled in $136.4 billion, while the current account deficit widened to $7 billion on a larger trade gap.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India’s emblem on the gate of its headquarters. The RBI reported a $20.8 billion balance-of-payments surplus for July, driven by a $27.7 billion capital-account inflow led by NRI deposits.
articles.nri_angle: NRI deposits — surging to $33.5 billion in July from $1 billion a year ago — have become the decisive variable in India's external balance, with the September 30 window on concessional FCNR-B hedging now closing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HSBC, ICICI Lead GIFT City's $19.3 Billion NRI Lending Boom
articles.excerpt: Moneycontrol reported NRI-linked lending at $19.3 billion as banks use offshore GIFT City units to offer leveraged FCNR-B deposits, riding the RBI's hedging-cost subsidies.
articles.image_caption: The ICICI Bank branch at K.G. Marg in New Delhi. ICICI is among the lenders financing GIFT City's fast-growing NRI loan book, where a new deposit scheme is drawing heavy dollar inflows from overseas Indians.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in the Gulf and US are the direct beneficiaries: leveraged FCNR-B deposits through GIFT City offer dollar yields well above Western rates, but the September 30 window and rollover risk demand attention.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: J.B. Hunt Shares Sink 13% After Warning Q3 Earnings Will Fall
articles.excerpt: CFO Brad Delco said third-quarter earnings will fall 5% to 10% from the second quarter as $25 million in driver costs and surging diesel prices squeeze margins — a rare intra-quarter warning that sent the stock to its steepest drop of the year.
articles.nri_angle: Freight costs ripple into goods prices and retail/manufacturing margins, so investors can treat the diesel-driven intermodal pricing advantage as a portfolio signal even without direct exposure to trucking.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Retail Sales Rebound 1.2% in August as Consumers Keep Spending
articles.excerpt: Shoppers stepped up purchases of cars and back-to-school goods in August, Commerce Department data showed Wednesday, underscoring a resilient economy just as the Federal Reserve moved to raise interest rates.
articles.image_caption: A shopper browsing clothes at a US retail store. US retail sales rebounded 1.2% in August as consumers kept spending.
articles.nri_angle: Mainly financial: Fed rate hikes raise borrowing costs on US mortgages, auto loans and credit cards for Indian-American households, while strong consumer demand supports equity portfolios.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran War's One-Two Punch of Oil and Rates Costs U.S. Households $1,700 Each
articles.excerpt: A Moody's Analytics tally puts the total cost of the U.S.-Iran conflict at about $1,760 per American household — $930 of it from energy, $425 from higher interest rates, and $405 from military spending.
articles.image_caption: A customer fills up at an Exxon station, with gasoline prices displayed on the sign. Moody's Analytics estimates the US-Iran war has cost American households about ,760 each in higher energy and borrowing costs.
articles.nri_angle: Higher fuel, borrowing, and grocery costs hit diaspora households — many concentrated in car-dependent suburbs with long commutes — exactly like every other American family.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NZ Super Fund, World's Top-Performing Sovereign Wealth Fund, Warns Equity Pullback Looms
articles.excerpt: The Guardians of New Zealand Superannuation, managers of the NZ$93 billion fund with 9.93% average annual returns over two decades, say US-driven equity gains won't repeat — and have cut their own return expectations accordingly.
articles.image_caption: Auckland, New Zealand. The NZ3 billion NZ Super Fund, headquartered in Auckland, has cut its long-term equity return assumptions, warning global equities are overvalued.
articles.nri_angle: Indian diaspora retirement savers heavily weighted to US equities face the same valuation risk the world's top sovereign wealth fund is now warning about.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Is Hitting Paychecks Before Payrolls, New Labor Data Show
articles.excerpt: Research from Apollo, Stanford and a 138-million-worker study finds pay growth running slower in AI-exposed occupations — with the lowest-paid workers taking the largest hit — even as employment holds steady.
articles.image_caption: An empty office chair carries a 'Replaced by AI' sign at a desk with a phone, computer mouse and eyeglasses. New labor research finds AI's measurable impact so far is showing up in slower wage growth and entry-level hiring freezes rather than in mass layoffs.
articles.nri_angle: No natural India-specific angle; the data cover the U.S. labor market broadly.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Paytm Shares Slide as NPCI Confirms 0.4% UPI Fee Above Rs 2,000
articles.excerpt: India's payments authority will levy the first-ever merchant fee on high-value UPI transactions from October 15, a day after the government shielded smaller payments from charges — and investors are repricing Paytm's earnings power.
articles.image_caption: A Paytm-branded markets graphic from The Economic Times. Paytm parent One 97 Communications fell more than 2.5% on Tuesday after the NPCI announced a 0.4% UPI fee on merchant payments above Rs 2,000.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who use UPI during India visits and diaspora investors in Indian fintech will feel the pricing and valuation shifts as the fee regime takes effect.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's August Exports Surge 25.4% as Trade Deficit Narrows Sharply
articles.excerpt: Exports hit $82.68 billion in August while a 57% plunge in gold imports helped push the overall deficit down to $9.41 billion.
articles.image_caption: A container ship at an Indian port. India’s merchandise exports rose 25.4% in August while the trade deficit narrowed sharply to $26.86 billion.
articles.nri_angle: Strong export data supports the India growth story that diaspora investors track in portfolios and remittance decisions; the gold import collapse also hints at changing festive-season buying behaviour among Indian households.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oil Prices Climb as Saudi Pipeline Outage and Houthi Advances Deepen Supply Fears
articles.excerpt: Brent crude traded near $108 a barrel on Tuesday as the shutdown of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and fresh Houthi attacks on the kingdom compounded fears of a prolonged supply squeeze.
articles.image_caption: Oil pumpjacks. Oil prices climbed after a Saudi pipeline outage and Houthi advances deepened supply concerns.
articles.nri_angle: For US households, the oil spike lands directly at the pump and in household bills while energy-heavy portfolios get a lift — a reminder to check exposure to fuel prices.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IT Stocks Rally as AI Leaders Back Slower Development; Nifty IT Jumps
articles.excerpt: Shares of Infosys, TCS and Wipro surged as the Nifty IT index jumped 5% after Anthropic's Dario Amodei called for pacing AI development, a stance quickly endorsed by Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Demis Hassabis.
articles.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange building in Mumbai. The Nifty IT index jumped 5% as shares of Infosys, TCS and Wipro surged after global AI leaders called for slowing the pace of AI development.
articles.nri_angle: The rebound matters to diaspora investors who hold Infosys and Wipro ADRs in US retirement accounts, and to Indian-American tech professionals wrestling with the same AI-disruption question.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Asian Stocks Hold Firm as AI Rebound Offsets Oil, Fed Hike Fears
articles.excerpt: Asian equities steadied on Tuesday as a tech rebound driven by calls to slow AI development balanced pressure from surging oil prices, a 10-year Treasury yield at 5%, and expectations of a Fed rate hike this week.
articles.image_caption: The market centre inside the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Asian equities steadied on Tuesday as a rebound in AI-linked shares offset surging oil prices and rising bond yields.
articles.nri_angle: For investors across the Indian diaspora, 5% Treasury yields pull capital away from emerging-market equities while costlier fuel feeds inflation back home in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
